title: TEST ONLY — MouseScript
profile: Knowledge-transfer learner; understands Python functions but overgeneralises familiar syntax.
goal: Implement a tiny mouse command language, connecting mechanisms with the RPG without copying project instructions into Library articles.

sessions.title: Commands before a compiler course
sessions.learner_prediction: A list of commands means we need classes and a full compiler immediately.
sessions.learner_attempt: Interpret MOVE 2 and SQUEAK hello by splitting a line.
sessions.observation: A small dispatch function handles the initial two commands.
sessions.correction: The simplest grammar can start with explicit tokens and a few branches.

decision.choice: Start with one command per line
decision.reason: It offers a runnable prediction before advanced abstractions.

sessions.unresolved: Do not introduce recursion before a nested-language need exists.
sessions.next_action: Predict position after MOVE 2 then MOVE -1, and inspect the result.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: Splitting cannot preserve a phrase
sessions.learner_prediction: str.split preserves quoted phrases just like a shell.
sessions.observation: Ordinary split yields multiple pieces and retains quote characters.
sessions.correction: Lexing rules are defined by the language; Python split is not a shell lexer.

decision.choice: Define quote and escape behaviour before choosing a tokenizer
decision.reason: The grammar should drive implementation rather than accidental library behaviour.

sessions.unresolved: Using shlex is a possible implementation choice only if its rules match the intended grammar.
sessions.next_action: Test an empty quoted phrase and an unmatched quote.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: An AST is not execution
sessions.learner_prediction: Building an AST has already moved the mouse twice.
sessions.learner_attempt: Represent REPEAT 2 { MOVE 1 } as a nested syntax node.
sessions.observation: The tree is data; no movement occurs until an evaluator visits it.
sessions.correction: Parsing and execution are distinct phases.

decision.reason: A printed tree helps connect nested data with familiar dictionaries/lists.

sessions.unresolved: No arbitrary Python eval or exec is authorised or needed.
sessions.next_action: Inspect the AST then execute it against a fresh state and compare position.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.

sessions.title: Transfer to the kitten
sessions.learner_prediction: Reusing an article means copying the whole kitten combat lesson.
sessions.learner_attempt: Use the RPG's state-factory pattern to isolate two script executions.
sessions.observation: Fresh state prevents one run's variables and movement leaking into the other.
sessions.correction: Transfer the mechanism and link the reusable explanation; project narrative stays in its own Journey.

decision.choice: Reuse state ownership and return-value concepts
decision.reason: The same knowledge explains independence without coupling both project routes.

sessions.unresolved: Recursive programs need a bounded execution budget before introduction; no unbounded recursion is tested.
sessions.next_action: Run the same AST against two states, then vary one variable and inspect the other.
sessions.evidence_boundary: All learner activity is scripted simulation. Artifacts may be executed by the lab runner; that does not prove a human learner executed or understood them.
